mainTopic: The laws and origin of the נר חנוכה: fuel, relighting, number of lights, placement, and the miracle of the oil
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of wicks and oils that are unfit for שבת. רב allows them for the נר חנוכה even on שבת. רבי ירמיה explains that, in רב's view, a light that went out need not be relit and its light may not be used. A story follows about אביי, who accepted this teaching only when he heard it in the name of רבי יוחנן. The גמרא then defends the rule that a light that went out need not be relit, and defines how long the lights must burn. A ברייתא gives the levels of the מצוה, including the מחלוקת between בית שמאי (start with eight and go down) and בית הלל (start with one and go up), along with two explanations of their reasons. The גמרא teaches that the light is placed outside the doorway and that a separate light is needed for ordinary use. It then tells the story of the miracle of the oil. Finally, a משנה about fire damage leads to a proof, which is then rejected, about how high the נר חנוכה should be placed. A new teaching from רבי תנחום begins, and its content comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the second opinion's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens at the end of the reasoning for the middle opinion: if the light goes out, one need not relight it, but it is permitted to use its light.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it goes out, one is not obligated to deal with it, and it is permitted to use its light.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the גמרא mid-sentence. It is finishing the explanation of why the second opinion allows these wicks for חנוכה on weekdays but not on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because one does not have to relight a light that went out, there is no need to use good wicks from the start, so weekdays are fine. But because one may use the light, on שבת a person might tilt or fix a poorly burning wick to use the light. So on שבת these wicks are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: obligated to attend to it (to relight it)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new opinion. It is the tail end of the reasoning given on the previous page for the middle view, which allows these wicks on weekdays and forbids them on שבת.

phrases.english: one is not obligated to attend to it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a light that went out (כבתה); those words come just before this amud begins.

phrases.english: and it is permitted to use its light.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ, וּמוּתָּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the middle opinion begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Middle view: no need to relight, and using the light is permitted. So these wicks are allowed on weekdays but not on שבת.

steps.title: רב's view: unfit wicks are fine for חנוכה even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that wicks and oils forbidden for שבת lights may be used for חנוכה on both weekdays and שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב מתנה, and some say רבי זירא said in the name of רב: the wicks and oils that חכמים said may not be lit on שבת may be lit on חנוכה, both on weekdays and on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third, most lenient opinion, that of רב. He allows the unfit wicks and oils for חנוכה at all times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbade these wicks for חנוכה entirely, and the second allowed them only on weekdays. רב goes furthest and allows them even on שבת. The two names given for the source (רב מתנה or רב) are just a disagreement about who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: both on a weekday and on שבת

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Matnah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav:
the wicks and oils about which the Sages said
one may not light with them on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Referring to the list in the משנה of במה מדליקין.

phrases.english: one may light with them on Chanukah,
both on a weekday and on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a third, more lenient opinion after the first two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfit wicks and oils are allowed for נר חנוכה even on שבת.

steps.title: What is רב's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks why רב permits these wicks even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: What is רב's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks for the logic behind רב's lenient ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees these wicks are forbidden for ordinary שבת lights, because one might adjust them. So we need to know why that worry does not apply to חנוכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: What is Rav's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב is not worried that a person will adjust the wick on שבת.

steps.title: רב holds no relighting and no using its light
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that a חנוכה light that went out need not be relit, and that it is forbidden to use its light.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if it goes out, one is not obligated to relight it, and it is forbidden to use its light.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers his own question by giving רב's two underlying principles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no relighting is needed, one does not have to choose good wicks from the start. Since one may not use the light at all, there is no reason to tilt or fix the wick on שבת. That removes the worry that forbids these wicks for regular שבת lights.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. View 1: must relight and may use the light, so these wicks are never allowed. View 2: no relighting but may use the light, so they are allowed only on weekdays. רב: no relighting and may not use the light, so they are always allowed.

phrases.english: He holds: if it went out, one is not obligated to attend to it,
and it is forbidden to use its light.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כָּבְתָה אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No duty to relight, and using the light is forbidden. So there is no reason to adjust the wick, even on שבת.

steps.title: אביי accepts the teaching only in רבי יוחנן's name
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejected this explanation when he heard it in the name of רבי ירמיה, accepted it in the name of רבי יוחנן, and wished he had learned it from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן said it before אביי in the name of רבי ירמיה, and he did not accept it. When רבין came, רבנן said it before אביי in the name of רבי יוחנן, and he accepted it. אביי said: had I merited, I would have learned this teaching from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how אביי reacted to this teaching depending on whose name it was said in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same idea was rejected under a less authoritative name and accepted under the great name of רבי יוחנן. אביי then expressed regret that he had not taken it in earlier.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it before Abaye
in the name of Rabbi Yirmeya, and he did not accept it.
When Ravin came (from Eretz Yisrael)
the Rabbis said it before Abaye
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, and he accepted it.
He said: Had I merited,
I would have learned this teaching from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about how רבי ירמיה's explanation of רב was received.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי ultimately accepted the teaching once it came in רבי יוחנן's name.

steps.title: But he did learn it in the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי regretted anything, since he did end up learning the teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did learn it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's regret. In the end he accepted and learned the teaching, so what did he lose?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is aimed at the words 'had I merited.' The outcome was the same, so the regret seems pointless.

phrases.english: But he did learn it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא גַּמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's statement of regret.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He ended up with the teaching anyway, so there is nothing to regret.

steps.title: Learning in youth sticks better
steps.stepSummary: The difference is that what one learns when young is remembered better.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is for learning done in one's youth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that learning something early, when young, stays with a person better than learning it later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי did gain the knowledge. But if he had accepted it right away, it would have been rooted more firmly in his memory.

phrases.english: The difference is for the learning of one's youth.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ לְגִירְסָא דְיַנְקוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning it later is just as good.
steps.terutzMaskana: Learning in youth is retained better, so the earlier chance was lost.

steps.title: Challenge: the מצוה lasts until the market empties
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the מצוה lasts from sunset until people leave the market. This suggests that a light that went out must be relit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it goes out, one is not obligated to relight it? Raise a contradiction: its מצוה is from sunset until the feet leave the market. Does this not mean that if it went out, one must relight it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea, held by both רב and the middle view, that a חנוכה light that went out need not be relit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the מצוה a time span. The simple reading is that the light must stay lit for that whole span, so if it goes out early, one must relight it.

keyTerms.meaning: the feet leave the market (traffic ends)

phrases.english: And if it went out, one is not obligated to attend to it?
Raise a contradiction:
Its מצוה is from when the sun sets
until the feet leave the market.
Does it not mean that if it went out,
he goes back and relights it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָבְתָה אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the הלכה and challenges the principle that no relighting is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule כָּבְתָה אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A required time span implies the light must burn the whole time, so relighting would be needed.

steps.title: The time span is for lighting late
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that if one did not light at sunset, one may still light until the market empties.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means that if he did not yet light, he may still light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets the ברייתא. The time span is the window for lighting, not a requirement to keep the light burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the ברייתא says nothing about a light that went out. So the rule that no relighting is needed stands.

keyTerms.meaning: that if he did not light

phrases.english: No: that if he did not light, he may still light.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּאִי לָא אַדְלֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The time span means the light must keep burning, so relight if it goes out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time span is the window in which a late lighting is still valid.

steps.title: Or: the time span sets the amount of oil
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the ברייתא tells how much oil to use, enough to burn until the market empties.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, it refers to its measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to read the ברייתא. It sets how much fuel the light must have when lit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One must put in enough oil to last the whole span. But if the light goes out early anyway, one does not need to relight it.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that a light which went out need not be relit survives. The time span in the ברייתא is either the window for lighting or the amount of oil needed.

phrases.english: Alternatively, it refers to its measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי לְשִׁיעוּרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time span defines how much oil is needed, not a duty to relight.

steps.title: How long is 'until the feet leave the market'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the phrase from the ברייתא again and asks how long that time is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until the feet leave the market. Until how long is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the phrase from the ברייתא to define it more exactly. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from whether one must relight to defining the time span itself. The repeated quote is the starting point for a new question.

phrases.english: Until the feet leave the market.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא's words here so it can ask what they mean.

phrases.english: And until how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁתִּכְלֶה רֶגֶל מִן הַשּׁוּק. וְעַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the challenge to defining a term in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of the time span.

steps.title: Until the תרמודאי traders leave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן defines the time as when the תרמודאי traders leave the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: until the feet of the תרמודאי leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a real-life marker: the time when the תרמודאי wood-sellers, the last people in the market, go home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sellers stayed late so people who ran out of wood could still buy some. When they leave, the street is truly empty and no passersby remain to see the light.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the time span for the חנוכה lights, which matters for how much oil to use and until when one may still light.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Until the feet of the Tarmodai leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד דְּכָלְיָא רִיגְלָא דְתַרְמוֹדָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The time ends when the תרמודאי wood sellers leave the market.

steps.title: Three levels of the מצוה of חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the basic מצוה of חנוכה and two higher levels of doing it beautifully.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: The basic מצוה of חנוכה is one light for a man and his whole household. Those who are meticulous (מהדרין) light one light for each person. And the most meticulous of the meticulous (מהדרין מן המהדרין) do the following:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא that lists levels of the מצוה of נר חנוכה. The last line introduces the highest level, and the details come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic obligation is small: one light for the whole house each night. The מהדרין go further and light one for each person. The phrase 'מהדרין מן המהדרין' sets up a still higher level, which בית שמאי and בית הלל will define differently.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Sages taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
One light for a man and his household. This is the basic מצוה.
People who are meticulous and beautify the מצוה.
The most meticulous of the meticulous, the highest level.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The מצוה of Hanukkah is a light for a man and his household.
And the meticulous light one light for each and every person.
And the most meticulous of the meticulous:
phrases.notes: This sets up the dispute that follows.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִצְוַת חֲנוּכָּה, נֵר אִישׁ וּבֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how long the light must burn to a new ברייתא about how many lights to light.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The basic מצוה is one light per household. מהדרין light one per person. A higher level, מהדרין מן המהדרין, also exists.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on decreasing or increasing the lights
steps.stepSummary: For the highest level, בית שמאי say to light eight and go down each night. בית הלל say to light one and go up each night.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: On the first day one lights eight, and from then on he lights one fewer each night. בית הלל say: On the first day one lights one, and from then on he adds one each night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving a מחלוקת about what the highest level looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the number of lights should change every night. They disagree about the direction. בית שמאי count down from eight to one, and בית הלל count up from one to eight.
steps.whyThisMatters: The practice today follows בית הלל: one light on the first night, adding one each night.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
On the first day one lights eight,
from then on he gradually decreases.
And Beit Hillel say:
On the first day one lights one,
from then on he gradually increases.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן מַדְלִיק שְׁמֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the highest level that step 13 introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: start with eight and decrease. בית הלל: start with one and increase.

steps.title: First explanation: counting the days ahead or the days already passed
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports that two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל explained the reasons differently. The first says בית שמאי count the days still to come, and בית הלל count the days already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Two אמוראים in מערבא (ארץ ישראל) disagreed about this: רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא. One said: בית שמאי's reason is that the lights match the days that are still coming. בית הלל's reason is that the lights match the days that have already gone out.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא reports a disagreement between two אמוראים about the reasons behind the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל. This step gives the first of their two explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this explanation, both sides count days. They only disagree about which days to count. בית שמאי count how many days remain: eight on the first night, then seven. בית הלל count how many days have arrived so far: one on the first night, then two.

keyTerms.meaning: The days still coming, the days that remain.
The days that have gone out, the days already reached.

steps.confusionAlert: 'הימים היוצאין' does not mean days that are still leaving in the future. It means days that have already been reached and passed. That is why the count goes up.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Two amoraim in the West disagreed about this:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida.
One said: the reason of Beit Shammai
is that it matches the incoming days,
and the reason of Beit Hillel
is that it matches the outgoing days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ תְּרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: בית שמאי match the lights to the remaining days, and בית הלל match them to the days already reached.

steps.title: Second explanation: the bulls of סוכות versus rising in holiness
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא says בית שמאי model the lights on the bulls of סוכות, which decrease each day. בית הלל follow the rule that in holy matters we go up, not down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: בית שמאי's reason is that it matches the bulls of the festival of סוכות. בית הלל's reason is that we go up in holiness and do not go down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second explanation of the same מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here בית שמאי have a source pattern: the קרבנות of סוכות, where one fewer bull is brought each day. בית הלל rely on a general principle: מעלין בקודש ואין מורידין, so holiness should only increase.

keyTerms.meaning: The bulls brought as קרבנות on סוכות, one fewer each day.
We go up in holiness and do not go down.

steps.confusionAlert: The bulls of סוכות start at thirteen, not eight. בית שמאי borrow only the pattern of going down each day, not the actual numbers.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle מעלין בקודש ואין מורידין appears in many places in ש״ס, far beyond חנוכה.

phrases.english: And one said: the reason of Beit Shammai
is that it matches the bulls of the festival,
and the reason of Beit Hillel
is that we go up in holiness and do not go down.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי כְּנֶגֶד פָּרֵי הַחַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from the one in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second view: בית שמאי follow the pattern of פרי החג, and בית הלל follow מעלין בקודש ואין מורידין.

steps.title: Two elders in צידן who acted on each view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports two elders in צידן. One followed בית שמאי and one followed בית הלל, and each gave the reasons from the second explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There were two elders in צידן. One acted like בית שמאי, and one acted like בית הלל. One gave the reason for his practice that it matches the bulls of the festival. The other gave the reason that we go up in holiness and do not go down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing real people who acted on these views. The reasons they gave match the second explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story adds real-life support for the second set of reasons: פרי החג for בית שמאי and מעלין בקודש for בית הלל. It shows that these reasons were actually used by people who kept these practices.

keyTerms.meaning: צידן (Sidon), a city north of ארץ ישראל.
Gives a reason for his position.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the מחלוקת. One is about counting the remaining days versus the days already reached. The other is about פרי החג versus מעלין בקודש. The elders in צידן support the second.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Hana said that Rabbi Yohanan said:
There were two elders in Sidon.
One acted like Beit Shammai
and one acted according to the words of Beit Hillel.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִדְבָרָיו כְּנֶגֶד פָּרֵי הַחַג,
phrases.english: This one gave a reason for his practice: matching the bulls of the festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִדְבָרָיו דְּמַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵין מוֹרִידִין.
phrases.english: and that one gave a reason for his practice: we go up in holiness and do not go down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁנֵי זְקֵנִים הָיוּ בְּצַיְדָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second explanation from step 16 with a report of actual practice.
steps.raayaObject: The second explanation of the reasons: פרי החג for בית שמאי and מעלין בקודש for בית הלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A report from רבי יוחנן about two elders in צידן who acted on these reasons.

steps.title: The נר חנוכה belongs outside the doorway
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that the מצוה is to place the נר חנוכה at the entrance of the house, on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: It is a מצוה to place the נר חנוכה at the entrance of one's house, on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: where to put the נר חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The best place is outside the doorway, where people passing by will see it. This shows that the light is meant to be seen by the public.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
It is a מצוה to place the Hanukkah light
at the entrance of his house, on the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נֵר חֲנוּכָּה מִצְוָה לְהַנִּיחָהּ עַל פֶּתַח בֵּיתוֹ מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the location of the light instead of the number of lights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נר חנוכה is placed at the entrance of the house, on the outside.

steps.title: Placing the light upstairs or in a time of danger
steps.stepSummary: Someone who lives upstairs places the light in a window facing the street. In a time of danger, placing it on one's table is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he lived in an upper story, he places it in the window that is next to the public domain. And in a time of danger, he places it on his table, and that is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives two exceptions to the rule of placing the light outside the door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person cannot reach the street easily, he still tries to show the light to the public through a window facing the street. When showing the light in public is dangerous, he lights it inside on his table, and he still fulfills the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of danger, for example when lighting is forbidden by the authorities.
And that is enough for him.

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is to show the light to the public: outside the door, or at a street-facing window if one lives upstairs. In danger, lighting on one's table inside is enough.

phrases.english: If he lived in an upper story,
he places it in the window next to the public domain.
And in a time of danger,
he places it on his table, and that is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה דָּר בַּעֲלִיָּיה מַנִּיחָהּ בַּחַלּוֹן הַסְּמוּכָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds exceptions to the placement rule from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone living upstairs places the light in a window facing the street. In danger, placing it on his table is enough.

steps.title: An extra light is needed for ordinary use
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that you need another light so you can use its light. A bonfire is enough, but an אדם חשוב still needs a separate light.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You need another light so you can use its light. If there is a bonfire, you don't need one. If he is an important person, even though there is a bonfire, he needs another light.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical rule. Since you may not use the נר חנוכה for your own needs, you should light a separate light for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra light protects you from accidentally using the נר חנוכה for personal needs. A bonfire already gives you usable light, so no extra light is needed. An אדם חשוב does not normally work by a bonfire's light, so he would end up using the נר חנוכה, and he still needs a separate light.

keyTerms.meaning: another light, a second lamp for ordinary use
to make use of its light

steps.confusionAlert: The extra light is not an additional מצוה light. It exists so that you do not use the real נר חנוכה for personal needs.

phrases.english: Rava said: one needs another light
to make use of its light.
And if there is a bonfire, he does not need one.
And if he is an important person,
even though there is a bonfire,
he needs another light.
phrases.notes: An important person does not normally use a bonfire's light.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: צָרִיךְ נֵר אַחֶרֶת לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical detail to the laws of placing the light, especially the case of lighting on the table in a time of danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You need a separate light for ordinary use. A bonfire is enough, except for an אדם חשוב.

steps.title: What is חנוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חנוכה is and why it is celebrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is חנוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a basic question about the reason for the holiday. This line sets up the next step, where a ברייתא answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with the details of lighting. Now it steps back to ask what event the holiday commemorates, so we understand why we light at all.

phrases.english: What is Chanukah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חֲנוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from technical laws to the basic reason for the holiday.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the holiday of חנוכה, and why was it established?

steps.title: Eight days with no eulogies or fasting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from מגילת תענית teaches that from כ״ה כסלו there are eight days of חנוכה, when one may not eulogize or fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבנן taught: On כ״ה כסלו, the days of חנוכה are eight. On them one may not eulogize and one may not fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives the date and the length of the holiday and says it is a time of joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the answer sets the basic facts: the holiday starts on כ״ה כסלו and lasts eight days. Because these are happy days, הספד and תענית are forbidden. The next step explains why.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
On the twenty-fifth of Kislev
the days of Chanukah are eight,
on which one may not eulogize
and on which one may not fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכ״ה בְּכִסְלֵיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to 'מאי חנוכה'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חנוכה is eight days starting כ״ה כסלו, and eulogies and fasting are forbidden on them.

steps.title: The miracle of the jug of oil
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the story: the יוונים made the oils טמא, and one sealed jug was found with enough oil for one day. It burned for eight days, and the next year the days were set as holidays with הלל and הודאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the יוונים entered the היכל, they made all its oils impure. When the kingdom of בית חשמונאי grew strong and defeated them, they searched and found only one jug of oil sealed with the seal of the כהן גדול, with enough to light for only one day. A miracle happened and they lit from it for eight days. The next year they established these days and made them festive days with הלל and הודאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the story behind the holiday. This completes the answer to 'What is Chanukah?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiday remembers the miracle of the oil in the היכל. The seal of the כהן גדול showed the oil was still pure. The holiday was set the following year, and it is marked with הלל and הודאה, not with sacrifices or a ban on work.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sanctuary of the בית המקדש
the seal of the High Priest, proof of purity

steps.whatToRemember: חנוכה remembers the miracle of the one pure jug of oil that lasted eight days. It was set as a holiday of הלל and הודאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic Talmudic source for the reason behind חנוכה and its eight days of lighting.

phrases.english: For when the Greeks entered the Sanctuary,
they made impure all the oils in the Sanctuary.
And when the Hasmonean kingdom grew strong and defeated them,
they searched and did not find
anything except one jug of oil

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מוּנָּח בְּחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: that was lying with the seal of the High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה בּוֹ אֶלָּא לְהַדְלִיק יוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and it held only enough to light for one day.
A miracle was done with it,
and they lit from it for eight days.
The following year they established them
and made them festive days with Hallel and thanksgiving.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ יְוָוֽנִים לַהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the eight days just mentioned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חנוכה remembers the miracle of the pure oil lasting eight days, and was set as a time of הלל and הודאה.

steps.title: A משנה about fire damage: the spark and the camel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from נזיקין. A smith is liable for sparks that cause damage. A camel owner is liable if his flax catches fire from a store's lamp. But if the storekeeper put his lamp outside, the storekeeper is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: A spark that comes out from under a hammer, goes out, and causes damage, the smith is liable. A camel loaded with flax passes through the public domain, its flax goes into a store, catches fire from the storekeeper's lamp, and sets the building on fire: the camel owner is liable. If the storekeeper put his lamp outside, the storekeeper is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a משנה from another מסכתא about damages. This sets up the next steps, which use this משנה to learn about the נר חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability falls on whoever acted where he had no right to. The camel owner's flax entered the store, where it did not belong, so he pays. If the storekeeper placed his lamp outside in the public street, he was the one out of place, so he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned there, in a משנה elsewhere

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
A spark that comes out from under the hammer
and went out and caused damage: he is liable.
A camel that is loaded with flax
and it is passing through the public domain,
and its flax went into the store
and caught fire from the storekeeper's lamp

phrases.aramaic: וְהִדְלִיק אֶת הַבִּירָה — בַּעַל הַגָּמָל חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and set the building on fire: the camel owner is liable.

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחַ חֶנְוָנִי אֶת נֵרוֹ מִבְּחוּץ — חֶנְוָנִי חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: If the storekeeper placed his lamp outside, the storekeeper is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: גֵּץ הַיּוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת הַפַּטִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the laws of נר חנוכה by bringing in an outside משנה that will turn out to matter for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever was out of place pays: the camel owner if the flax entered the store, the storekeeper if his lamp was outside.

steps.title: רבי יהודה exempts a נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that if the lamp outside was a נר חנוכה, the storekeeper is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: With a נר חנוכה, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the same משנה. רבי יהודה adds an exception for the storekeeper whose outside lamp was a נר חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a storekeeper who puts a lamp outside is liable, because he had no right to put it there. A נר חנוכה, though, is supposed to be placed outside, so he was allowed to put it there and does not pay.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With a Chanukah lamp, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּנֵר חֲנוּכָּה פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the storekeeper's liability in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A storekeeper whose נר חנוכה outside burned the flax is exempt.

steps.title: Learning that the נר חנוכה belongs below ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבינא, in the name of רבה, learns from רבי יהודה that the מצוה is to place the נר חנוכה within ten טפחים of the ground. Otherwise the storekeeper should have placed it higher than a camel and its rider.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said in the name of רבה: This shows that the נר חנוכה should, as a מצוה, be placed within ten טפחים. For if you think it may go above ten, let the camel owner say to him: You should have placed it above the camel and its rider!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws a new הלכה out of רבי יהודה's ruling. He argues that the storekeeper is only exempt if the מצוה requires placing the lamp low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נר חנוכה could be placed high, the storekeeper could have put it above a camel and its rider and avoided the damage, so he would not be exempt. Since רבי יהודה does exempt him, it must be that the מצוה is to place the lamp low, within ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: within ten טפחים (handbreadths) of the ground
if it would enter your mind, if you thought

phrases.english: Ravina said in the name of Rabba:
This shows that the Chanukah lamp
should, as a מצוה, be placed within ten (handbreadths).
For if you thought it may be placed above ten,
let (the camel owner) say to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה לָךְ לְהַנִּיחַ לְמַעְלָה מִגָּמָל וְרוֹכְבוֹ!
phrases.english: You should have placed it above the camel and its rider!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבָּה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a law about the height of the נר חנוכה from רבי יהודה's exemption.
steps.raayaObject: That the מצוה is to place the נר חנוכה within ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's exemption of the storekeeper in the נזיקין משנה.

steps.title: Maybe the exemption is so people won't skip the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: perhaps a high placement is allowed, and רבי יהודה exempts the storekeeper only because too heavy a burden would make people avoid the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps: if you trouble him too much, he will come to hold back from the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's proof by offering a different reason for רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed the only reason for the exemption is that the lamp must be low. The גמרא suggests another reason: if we demand that he lift it above a camel and rider, it becomes too much trouble and people may stop lighting. So the exemption does not prove the lamp must be within ten.

keyTerms.meaning: to hold back from doing the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say the lamp must be high. It only shows that רבי יהודה's ruling does not prove the lamp must be low.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא tried to prove from רבי יהודה that the נר חנוכה must be within ten טפחים. The proof is rejected, because the exemption may come from not wanting to burden people and drive them away from the מצוה.

phrases.english: But perhaps:
if you trouble him too much,
he will come to hold back from the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 26 by offering another reason for רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that the lamp must be within ten. It does not decide the height question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the only reason for the exemption is a low-placement requirement. A concern that people would skip the מצוה could also explain it.

steps.title: Attribution chain opening a new teaching about the Chanukah lamp
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רב נתן בר מניומי publicly taught a ruling in the name of רבי תנחום. The ruling itself comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: רב נתן בר מניומי taught in the name of רבי תנחום:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It names who taught the upcoming ruling but does not state the ruling yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 left open whether placing the נר חנוכה up high is allowed. Now the גמרא brings a new teaching on the topic, passed down through three people: רבי תנחום taught it, רב נתן בר מניומי publicly taught it in his name, and רב כהנא reports it. The content arrives in the very next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or expounded publicly, usually in a public lecture
In the name of. It shows who the teaching originally came from.
The אמורא who reports this teaching
The original source of the teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a ruling in this line. It is only the chain of names. The actual statement about the נר חנוכה comes immediately after it.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Rav Natan bar Manyumi taught publicly
in the name of Rabbi Tanchum:

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup / attribution line for the next מימרא
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, דָּרֵשׁ רַב נָתָן בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the דחיה in Step 27 weakened the proof from רבי יהודה, the גמרא brings a separate, direct teaching on where to place the נר חנוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is stated on this amud. It only introduces a teaching from רבי תנחום, passed on by רב נתן בר מניומי and reported by רב כהנא.
